history.summary: DUPLICATE/OVERLAP: this temple is already documented in the dataset as file 2335.json, id 'sri-lakshmi-narasimha-swamy-temple-yadadri' ('Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Yadadri)'). Research notes: Telangana's most famous Vaishnavite shrine ('Telangana's Tirupati'), a Pancha Narasimha Kshetram on a hillock about 60 km from Hyderabad. Legend: sage Yadarishi meditated in a cave here and Vishnu appeared before him in five forms (Lakshmi Narasimha, Jwala, Gandabherunda, Yoga, Ugra); the cave remains the garbhagriha. In recent years the temple underwent a massive Agama-Shastra-based reconstruction in black granite (no steel/concrete) with a 90-foot rajagopuram and expanded queue complexes. Worship follows Vaikhanasa Agama; full-moon Lakshmi Narasimha Maha Yagam is a noted rite. CSV town 'Nalgonda' corrected: actual town is Yadagirigutta (also called Yadadri), Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district. CSV state 'Nalgonda' corrected: Telangana. CONFLICT: opening hours vary across sources (4:00 AM, 4:30 AM or 5:00 AM open; 9:00/9:30 PM close); nearest-station distances also vary (Raigiri 3-6 km, Bhongir 14 km).

name: Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
town_description: Yadagirigutta (also rendered Yadadri) is a temple town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, about 60-65 km from Hyderabad via NH163. It is built around the Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy hill shrine, with TSRTC buses, nearby railway stations at Raigiri (about 3-5 km) and Bhongir (about 14 km), and attractions like Surendrapuri and Bhongir Fort nearby.
